The '''1992–93 Bundesliga''' was the 30th season of the [[Bundesliga]], Germany's premier football league. It began on 14 August 1992<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=323483 |title=Schedule Round 1 |publisher=DFB |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608092228/https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=323483 |archive-date=8 June 2011 }}</ref> and ended on 5 June 1993.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=323845 |title=Archive 1992/1993 Round 34 |publisher=DFB |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608092254/https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=323845 |archive-date=8 June 2011 }}</ref> [[VfB Stuttgart]] were the defending champions.

==Competition format==
Every team played two games against each other team, one at home and one away. Teams received two points for a win and one point for a draw. If two or more teams were tied on points, places were determined by [[goal difference]] and, if still tied, by goals scored. The team with the most points were crowned champions while the three teams with the fewest points were relegated to [[2. Bundesliga]].

==Team changes to 1991–92==
[[Stuttgarter Kickers]], [[FC Hansa Rostock|Hansa Rostock]], [[MSV Duisburg]] and [[Fortuna Düsseldorf]] were relegated to the [[1992–93 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]] after finishing in the last four places. Due to a size reduction back to 18 teams, only two teams were promoted. These were [[KFC Uerdingen 05|Bayer 05 Uerdingen]], winners of the 2. Bundesliga Northern Division and [[1. FC Saarbrücken]], champions of the Southern Division.
